title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
description: Brute force to optimized: recursively simulating transactions versus directly summing every positive consecutive-day price difference.

sections.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II

content.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II

blocks.text: Problem Summary: Given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i, you may buy and sell the stock any number of times, but you must sell before buying again (only one share held at a time). Return the MAXIMUM total profit achievable.

blocks.caption: What goes in, what comes out

blocks.content: {"headers":["Aspect","Detail"],"rows":[["Input","prices, an array of daily stock prices"],["Output","Maximum total profit from any number of buy-sell transactions"],["Goal","Compute this in a single pass, without explicitly simulating trades"],["Constraints","1 <= prices.length <= 3*10^4"]]}

{"headers":["Signal in the problem","Pattern it points to"],"rows":[["\"Unlimited transactions, maximize total profit\"","The total achievable profit equals the sum of every consecutive day-to-day price increase"],["\"Buy low, sell high, repeatedly\"","Capture every single upward price movement, since selling right before any dip and re-buying right after captures the same total gain as any more complex multi-day hold"]]}

blocks.text: Since there is no limit on the number of transactions, the maximum achievable profit is exactly the sum of every day-to-day price INCREASE, since each such increase represents "buying the day before and selling the day of" a price rise, and unlimited transactions mean every single such rise can be captured independently.

blocks.title: Analogy: Capturing Every Uphill Stretch of a Hiking Trail's Elevation
blocks.text: Picture a hiking trail's daily elevation readings, and wanting the total elevation GAINED by only ever moving during uphill stretches (never counting downhill loss). Summing every single day-to-day increase in elevation gives exactly this total gain, and the same logic applies to capturing stock profit across every upward price movement.

blocks.caption: The maximum profit equals the sum of every single consecutive day-to-day price increase

blocks.text: Result: 7. Buy at 1, sell at 5 (profit 4); buy at 3, sell at 6 (profit 3); total 4+3=7, equal to the sum of every consecutive price increase.

Before trying to identify specific buy and sell days explicitly, notice that with unlimited transactions, the total achievable profit is mathematically identical to summing every day where the price went UP from the previous day, since any longer hold can be decomposed into consecutive daily buy-sell pairs with the same total gain.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: If price goes up on some day, that increase can always be captured by buying the day before and selling that day, an achievable transaction under the "sell before buying again" rule.

Observation 2: If a longer upward run occurs (prices strictly increasing for several days), capturing it as ONE buy-at-start, sell-at-end transaction gives the exact same total profit as capturing EACH day's individual increase separately (buy, sell, immediately rebuy, sell again, etc.), since the sum telescopes to the same total.

Observation 3: Since unlimited transactions are allowed, there is no cost or limitation to capturing every single day-to-day increase independently.

Observation 4: Therefore, the maximum total profit is simply the sum of prices[i] - prices[i-1] for every i where this difference is positive.
This leads to a single pass: sum prices[i] - prices[i-1] for every consecutive day pair where the price increased, giving the maximum total profit directly.
Recursively try every possible set of non-overlapping buy-sell transaction pairs, tracking the maximum total profit achievable.

items: From the current day, either skip it (move to the next day) or buy on this day, then recursively find the best day to sell afterward.
After selling, recursively consider further transactions from the day after selling.
Track the maximum total profit across all valid sequences of transactions.

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: Recursively trying every buy/sell/skip decision directly explores every possible trading strategy.
This costs exponential time without memoization, far more complex than necessary given the direct summation shortcut available.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: exponential without memoization (or O(n) with memoization on day and holding state, but still more complex than needed).
Space: O(n) recursion depth.
Limitation: recognizing that total profit equals the sum of all positive day-to-day differences reduces this to a single O(n) pass with no recursion or memoization needed at all.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text:
Why simulating transactions explicitly is unnecessary: any profitable multi-day hold can be decomposed into a sequence of single-day buy-sell-rebuy-sell operations with the identical total profit, since the gains telescope together.

The direct summation insight: since unlimited transactions are allowed, this decomposition is always achievable without any cost or restriction, meaning the SUM of every single positive day-to-day price difference IS the maximum achievable profit.

The single-pass implementation: simply iterate through consecutive day pairs, adding (prices[i] - prices[i-1]) to a running total whenever it is positive.

The core idea: total profit is exactly the sum of all daily upward price movements, computable in one linear pass with no recursion.
In a single pass, for each consecutive pair of days, if the price increased, add that increase to a running total profit. Return the total.

blocks.caption: Sum every positive consecutive-day price increase in a single pass

blocks.text: Since transactions are unlimited and there is no restriction against immediately re-buying right after selling, every single day-to-day price increase can be captured independently, regardless of whether it is part of a longer upward run. Summing prices[i] - prices[i-1] whenever positive exactly reconstructs the total gain from every such increase, matching the maximum achievable profit from any valid trading strategy.

blocks.text: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II is a strong example of recognizing a mathematical equivalence (total profit equals the sum of all positive daily differences) that completely bypasses the need to simulate any actual trading decisions.

items: Trying to explicitly track buy and sell days, overcomplicating a problem that has a much simpler direct summation solution.
Forgetting that unlimited transactions are what make this summation trick valid; this technique does NOT apply to the single-transaction version of the problem.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Case","Expected Behavior"],"rows":[["Prices strictly decreasing throughout","Returns 0, since no day-to-day increase ever occurs."],["Prices strictly increasing throughout","Returns prices[last] - prices[first], as the sum of every daily increase telescopes to this."]]}

blocks.text: Explicitly proving the equivalence ("any multi-day hold's profit telescopes into the sum of its daily increases, and unlimited transactions let us capture every increase independently") is the key insight that should be stated clearly before writing the one-line solution.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "unlimited transactions, maximize total profit", think: sum every single positive day-to-day price increase directly.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: Recursive transaction simulation is more complex than necessary; summing positive daily differences runs in O(n) time and O(1) space, the simplest and most efficient solution.

items: Pattern: total profit under unlimited transactions equals the sum of every positive consecutive-day price difference.
Core Idea: in a single pass, add prices[i] - prices[i-1] to a running total whenever it is positive.
Time: exponential (or O(n) with memoization) for explicit transaction simulation, O(n) for the direct summation approach.
Space: O(n) recursion depth versus O(1) extra.
Most Important Observation: unlimited transactions let every single daily price increase be captured independently, making direct summation exactly equivalent to optimal trading.
Interview Difficulty: a deceptively simple problem once the key mathematical equivalence is recognized.
One line memory trick: sum every positive day-to-day price increase.
